title: The Cartier equality for a finitely generated field extension
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves the Cartier equality: for a finitely generated field extension the differential module and the first homology of the naive cotangent complex are finite dimensional and their dimension difference equals the transcendence degree. The proof realises the field as the fraction field of a global complete intersection over the base field, then computes the naive cotangent complex of the field extension as homotopy equivalent to the two-term complex given by the relations and the differentials, using the homotopy invariance and localisation results for that complex. The transcendence degree is identified with the dimension of the complete intersection, which is the number of variables minus the number of relations, giving the stated equality.
